title: Four sheets, one readout
summary: What the ten days return, as the page's one paper moment: four folio sheets dealt from a stack, one per part of the written readout, each drawing the SHAPE of its part (structure only) above what it reads and its layer page, so 'a written readout' becomes something you can see and hold.

reference.site: Duolingo research reports (document thumbnails that carry a schematic of their own content) · approved Kelwin handover/U (the six assets as documents you keep)
reference.borrowed: A document shown as a page whose thumbnail is a small drawing of what is inside it, with its title and one line of what it covers beside it.
reference.kelwin: No thumbnails or photos: four full-size folio sheets on the paper surface, drawn in the kit's 1px classes, each part's drawing a structural specimen of its own logic (one message fraying into five; channels that reach pipeline and channels that leak; decisions against the evidence they rest on, gaps dashed; three fixes in order, the first in ink). Dealt from a stack, once. Every illustrative mark sits under one SpecimenTag.

motion: entrance: the section head fades and rises (kit). The set fades in as one stack on sheet 01's place (one layer's opacity, so no sheet ever shows through another), squared up and offset 6px per sheet; then 02, 03 and 04 are dealt out to their columns, 100ms apart, 640ms each (0.5–1.3s): opaque paper, transform only. The words under each sheet rise as it lands; the SpecimenTag fades in, then the foot's hairline draws and its line and link fade in (1.4–2.2s).
ambient: none — the drawings are still once dealt (the page's second play-once body moment is the FAQ's 01 opening).
interaction: the three layer links and the /reports link (kit hovers).
on the live site: the deal plays once when the section is 40% visible. Reduced motion: the laid-out set at once.
story: Answers 'what exactly do I get?' with the thing itself: the readout's four parts, each tied to the layer it reads, and the plan that orders them, paying off the homepage's 'Find your weakest layer' with 'The readout names your weakest layer first.'

notes: No red: the view's red is the header's Day 10 tick above and the FAQ's button below. The four drawings are structure-only specimens (no numbers, no names, no findings) under one SpecimenTag.
